title: Coverage Office Note: Charged Days a Payer Covers on Ancillary Items Paid from Resident Funds
content:
When a transfer from a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account paid an ancillary charge and the return of its payer-covered part is figured, the covered days of that charge come from **the days counted from the payer's start**. Those days follow the resident's payer, as the records of Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage and Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage show it.

## The rule

| What the resident's coverage records show | Days counted from the payer's start |
|---|---|
| a Medicare Part A episode is active | the charged days on or after the episode's coverage start date |
| no Part A episode is active and the Medical Assistance case is eligible | the charged days on or after the eligibility start date |
| the resident has neither payer | every charged day |

A one-time item counts its one day only when its service date falls on or after that start. A recurring service charge's days run from its first billed day, so the days on or after the start are its charged days less the days that fall before the start, and none where the start falls after its last billed day.

## Both sides of the start date (hypothetical dates)

| Charge | Payer's start | Days counted |
|---|---|---|
| one-time item, service date 16 March | Part A coverage start 17 March | 0 |
| one-time item, service date 17 March | Part A coverage start 17 March | 1 |
| recurring charge, 29 days from 3 March (3 to 31 March) | Part A coverage start 17 March | 15 (14 days fall before the start) |
| recurring charge, 29 days from 3 March | Part A coverage start 1 March | 29 |
| recurring charge, 12 days from 19 June (19 to 30 June) | no Part A episode; Medical Assistance eligible from 1 July | 0 |

## Basis Q&A

**The resident has both an active Part A episode and an eligible Medical Assistance case. Which start date counts?** The active Part A episode's coverage start date.

**The Part A episode has ended and the Medical Assistance case is eligible.** No Part A episode is active, so the eligibility start date counts.
